public_rationale: There is meaningful evidence against the categorical denial: Reuters documented an internal reasoning project predating the post, and OpenAI later disclosed substantial reasoning gains. Murati's June statement points the other way. Neither the later results nor the earlier qualitative reports establish the relevant internal capabilities on July 8. Calling the observation contradicted would require backdating September's measured gains or treating research activity itself as a breakthrough.
limitations: Internal capabilities were not comprehensively public.
The Reuters report relies partly on unnamed sources.
OpenAI's September comparisons are company evaluations.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI does not have a secret, unreleased breakthrough technology.

statement.excerpt: Yet, I have a counterpoint: no it doesn't.

from_speaker: OpenAI has something we don't know about
not much more advanced than those that are publicly-available
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that OpenAI did not already possess an unreleased system substantially more capable than its public models.
A research project or planned improvement alone does not establish possession of a breakthrough.
This is an assessment of the internal state at publication, July 8, 2024. There is no regular reporting period for internal capabilities, so I use that date as the observation date.
Later releases count decisively only if records establish that their substantial advantages already existed by the observation date.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable records describing OpenAI's internal systems at publication establish that they offered no substantial capability advance over its public systems.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Dated records establish that OpenAI already possessed an unreleased system with substantial capability advances at publication.
